newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50-1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50-1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 0.50 to 1.00 cent a lb lower on Tuesday, as traders expected prices to pull back after Monday's strong gains.

New York arabica futures ended sharply higher on Monday on news Colombia had closed coffee registrations for May and June shipments. Spot May ran up 6.90 cents per lb on the day, to 196.00 cents, after trading from 197.00 to 186.20. Second-month July settled 4.80 cents higher, at 177.00 cents, while the back months closed up 0.95 to 4.00.
The May/July switch ballooned to a hefty 19.00 cents, up from 16.90 cents at the close on Friday.
Technically, traders pegged May support at 192.00 cents, and said the spot contract would face strong resistance at the 200.00 marke.
Traders await the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock data due after today's close to better gauge the U.S. supply situation.

Coffee fell sharply a week-and-a half ago on talk of a 500,000 to 1.0-million bag rise in the March inventory, but traders now expect an increase of 250,000 to 350,000 bags from February's 1.54 million bags.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 80,828 bags as of April 11. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.

In other news, the chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, Jorge Cardenas, said late Monday that the counrtry's output totalled 10 million 60-kg bags in 1996/97 (April-March), down from about 14 million in the same 1995/96 period.
Elsewhere, stevedores at the key Brazilian port of Santos began a strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT Tuesday for indefinite period, bring loading and unloading of ships to a halt, a union official said.
The official said the stoppage comes as 25 ships are awaiting loading or unloading at Santos port and said that the strike could spread to a national level on Wednesday.
London robusta prices were broadly higher early Tuesday, but origin sales capped gains. LIFFE May was up $25 at the midday break, to $1,578 a tonne, after peaking at $1,585.

LIFFE reported on Monday March certified coffee stocks rose to 4,008 lots from 2,801 lots in February. Traders were not surprised by the sharp build in stocks given the heavy origin shipments following the recent market rally.
